$description: KinetixUI motion contract. Duration and easing VALUES and their intent ($description) live in tokens/primitives/motion.json, which Style Dictionary generates to every platform. This file is not a token source and Style Dictionary does not read it. It records how the tiers relate to the MX1 proposal, which duration + easing pairings are roles and whether a gate proves them, each role’s reduced-motion form, how each platform interprets the values, and which motion dimensions are deliberately not tokenised yet. scripts/check-motion-tokens.mjs holds it to the source; /docs/foundations renders it and MOTION.md explains it.

base.note: The MX1 brief calls this tier `normal`. The token is `base` on five platforms (CSS --duration-base, Tailwind duration-base, KinetixDuration.base); renaming it would break every consumer for no change in value, so the brief's word is documentation only.

slow.note: The MX1 brief proposes 400ms. The token is 500ms and Sheet's open uses it; moving it would change Sheet on every platform without a measured reason. Revisit only with a rendered comparison.

slower.note: Not in the MX1 tier table. Intended for loop periods; no loop reads it today (see the loop role).

reducedForms.shorten: The transition runs at ~0ms and reaches the same end state. State is never lost; only the interpolation goes.
reducedForms.crossfade: Spatial travel is replaced by an opacity change to the same end state.
reducedForms.rest: A loop stops at a static state that keeps its role and accessible name (Spinner ring, Skeleton at full opacity, still Marquee).
reducedForms.remove-travel: The element appears at its destination with no travel; colour or shape changes may still shorten.

selection-control.note: Switch only, on purpose: its thumb is a physical control, so the thumb's travel, the track colour and the halo all run on instant. It is not selection-state (fast), and the two are not to be normalised (owner decision 2026-10-17, re-confirmed for MX1b-1c). React MX1b-1c measured the thumb frame by frame in Chromium (forward only, no overshoot, mirrored in RTL, aria-checked first) and added the registry reduced form and a forced-colours thumb. MX1b-2 aligned Angular: the thumb and the track left base (300ms) for instant, measured frame by frame in Chromium (scripts/angular-selection-motion.mjs), and the thumb is drawn in CanvasText (GrayText when disabled) so forced colours no longer hide it.

overlay.note: Open on fast + enter, close on instant + exit: the exit is shorter because a dismissed surface should not linger. Repeated on React Dialog and Sheet's scrim; the motion-contract test proves each animate-in/out names a token duration, not that this pairing holds.

spatial.note: Large surfaces: Sheet opens on slow and closes on base. One React consumer and no rendered check, so it is recorded, not promoted.

properties: transform or logical inset of one shared indicator
selection-indicator.note: A single indicator travelling between selected items (Tabs, SegmentedControl). Being built for React in PR #388; not on main. Promote to observed when #388 merges and add its consumer; promote to proven when a rendered midpoint check covers it.

selection-state.note: Colour and surface change when a control becomes selected or unselected: Toggle, ToggleGroup items, Checkbox and Radio indicators. Owner decision 2026-10-17: fast (200ms). The semantic state changes at once; only the paint interpolates. Switch keeps selection-control (instant) unless a defect is shown. Adopted component by component from MX1b-1. Observed on React Toggle and ToggleGroup (MX1b-1a, which share toggleVariants): background, text and border colour on fast, measured in a browser. Observed on React Checkbox and RadioGroup (MX1b-1b): box fill, border and glyph colour on fast, and the tick, dash or dot fading in on fast (opacity). The Checkbox glyph leaves at once rather than fading, so a box going from mixed to unchecked never shows the tick on its way out. Promoted to proven when a second platform consumes it. MX1b-2 adopted it on Angular Checkbox, RadioGroup, Toggle and ToggleGroup: colour and edge on fast, the Checkbox glyph and the Radio dot fading on fast from their own layers, and the state layer kept on instant.

press-feedback.note: Immediate hover and press colour on buttons, toggles and rows. Today most of these React components name no duration and run on Tailwind's untokenised 150ms default (see the debt register in motion-contract.test.ts). Owner decision 2026-10-17: press feedback is instant (100ms) where it applies, and a change of selected state uses selection-state (fast). There is no global retiming; each component moves in its own slice. Observed on React Toggle and ToggleGroup (MX1b-1a): an inset box-shadow state layer (foreground 8% hover, 14% press) on instant, so it is told apart from selection by property; the expects below pin instant to the last slot, box-shadow. Checkbox and RadioGroup (MX1b-1b) put their existing 5px foreground halo (8% hover, 14% press) on instant the same way. Their box's own hover and press colour step (TOKENS.md, Selection controls) is kept and moves with the colour on fast; the halo is the immediate answer. MX1b-2 gave Angular Toggle and ToggleGroup the same inset layer (8% hover, 14% press) on instant, and kept the Angular Checkbox, Radio and Switch halo there.

loop.scope: Spinner, Skeleton, Marquee and the typing indicator, on every platform that ships them
loop.note: Loops have no destination, so the contract is their reduced form (a static rest), not a duration pair. Each loop keeps its own period (caret 1.25s, typing 1.2s, marquee 32s), set on the keyframe animation rather than a transition tier. `slower` (1000ms) is documented for loops but nothing reads it as a period today: InputOTP's caret pairs `animate-caret-blink` with the transition utility `duration-slower`, which does not change an animation's duration.

spring.reason: No component uses a spring on any platform. CSS has no spring timing function (only linear() approximations), while SwiftUI .spring(response:dampingFraction:), Compose spring(dampingRatio, stiffness) and Flutter SpringDescription take different parameters that do not map one to one. A shared spring token would be a fiction until a component needs one.
spring.addWhen: A component needs interruptible physical motion (drag release, sheet fling) on at least two platforms; then define the intent (e.g. 'settle') and each platform's native parameters, verified on that platform.

distance.reason: Enter offsets reuse the spacing scale (tailwindcss-animate slide-in-from-* take spacing steps); no separate distance token exists or is needed yet.
distance.addWhen: Two components need the same travel distance that is not a spacing step.

delay.reason: A delay is expressed as a duration token (e.g. the trailing edge of an indicator delayed by instant). No standalone delay tokens.
delay.addWhen: A delay is needed that is not one of the duration tiers, by at least two components.

stagger.reason: The only library stagger is the typing indicator's 150ms dot offset, hard-coded on React, SwiftUI, Compose and Flutter. One consumer does not justify a five-platform token.
stagger.addWhen: A second library component staggers (list or card entrance); then add motion.stagger.* and migrate the typing dots to it.

react.reducedMotion: Preset floor shortens every duration to 0.01ms; loops add motion-reduce:animate-none. Registry installs do not get the floor.

angular.reducedMotion: Per-component @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) blocks; no global floor yet.

swiftui.easing: exact (Animation.timingCurve with the same control points)

compose.reducedMotion: System animator duration scale (ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0) through family helpers
